# THE FOUR NAMES

*Four words have been carrying one thing: path, knot, glyph, card. They are
not synonyms. They are four depths of a single object, and only the first of
them is the object.*

---

## I · THE STACK

A card of the deck is a closed walk on the torus, generated by a winding
pair and nothing else. Every other name for it is that walk seen through a
further lens.

**The path.** The thing itself: a trajectory on the surface, closing on
itself after so many turns one way and so many the other. At the found
radius, root two, the path is a geodesic, straight in the surface's own
geometry and bent only by the shape of the space it walks in.

**The knot.** The path's topological type once the torus is carried into
three dimensions. A property held by the path, never the path itself. It is
also the first name that fails: where the strand count exceeds one the
figure is a link, several closed walks travelling together.

**The glyph.** The path's shadow, cast flat. A projection, and projections
lose. Crossings that were nowhere near each other on the surface meet on the
page, and the eye reads a tangle the walk never had.

**The card.** The container that carries the glyph to a person, exact at its
own depth and mute about everything above it.

Each name is a projection of the one before it: embed, project, print.
Something is lost at every step, and the card, furthest from the walk, is
the name that has done most of the speaking.

## II · WHAT THE ORDER SETTLES

Three things stop being coincidences once the walk is read as the primitive.

**The membership rule.** The twenty-seven are not twenty-seven shapes that
were chosen. They are the walks that close. At a non-rational slope the
strand winds forever, dense on the surface, an open thread that never
returns, and the deck already has a name for that country: the open water.
So the criterion for entry is homecoming, which is a property of walks
rather than a decision about forms. HOMECOMING stands fifth among the first
names. The ontology and the name-law say the same sentence.

**The Seed.** The loop that closes without ever winding. Read as a card it
is a permanent exception: the one with the empty plate, the figure that is
never struck, the entry every rule has to make room for. Read as a walk it
is the identity, obviously and necessarily. The deck's group structure
follows the same way, order twenty-seven with the Seed at its centre, every
counter an inverse, any two meeting in a third. Cards do not compose. Walks
do.

**The reading.** A spread of three is not three objects set side by side. It
is a route with three waypoints, and the moves between them are the deck's
own verbs: the counter, the becoming, the successor. Navigation as sentence,
with the closed walks as the places the sentence pauses into a word.

## III · WHERE THE SINGULAR FAILS

Where the greatest common divisor of the winding pair exceeds one, the
figure is not one path but several, closed and travelling together. The
singular noun breaks there, and it breaks honestly: such a card is more than
one journey at once, which is a reading rather than a defect. The words that
survive the plural are walk and route. Path does not.

## IV · WHAT THIS LEAVES ALONE

No name is retired here. Each of the four is exact at its own depth, and the
fault was never a wrong word but four right words used as one. The engine
derives paths, the topology reports knots and links, the renderer draws
glyphs, the interface deals cards, and a reading walks a route. Card stops
being wrong the moment it stops standing in for the walk.

The first names outrank all later canon and are untouched by this chart.
Nothing here renames a card, alters an arithmetic, or moves a seat.

## PROVENANCE

*Named 25 July 2026 at the architect's word. The seeing was already half
written: the Atlas, set down the day before, opens with paths and not glyphs
as the language, and closes by calling the card the straightest possible
walk that still comes home. This chart states the ordering that sentence
assumed. The stratification is named and not yet in force: the canon still
speaks of cards at every depth, and no pin holds the layers apart.*

---

*The walk is the thing. The rest are its shadows, each true at its own depth.*
